input.question: What was popular British opinion of the American Revolution?
input.ground_truth: Something that could be used to gauge popular opinion in that time was voting in the House of Commons. The last time any PM was defeated over issue of war and peace (until David Cameron on Syria) was in 1782 regarding the rebellious American colonies.

Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What was popular British opinion of the American Revolution?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big family. Some people in your family live in England, and some live in America. One day, the people in America decide they don’t want to listen to the rules from England anymore. They want to make their own rules.

Now, most people in England didn’t really care much about what the Americans were doing at first. Some people in England thought the Americans should just listen to the king, because England was like their big boss. But some other people in England thought, “Well, maybe they have a point,” but not many people in England really cared or talked about it a lot.

Most British people just went about their normal lives. They didn’t celebrate or get angry about the American Revolution. They were busy with their own things. Only a few important people in England, like the king and some leaders, really worried about what was happening in America.
